symmetric_qc_open_items: The amyloid-cascade CAUSAL DIRECTION (amyloid-first vs tau-first vs parallel-independent) is genuinely contested and explicitly held OPEN -- Jack et al 2013's own revision of Jack et al 2010 allows independent initiation; this document does not adjudicate it.

Amyloid may gate tau's spread RATE/magnitude (Hanseeuw 2019 beta=1.07 P=.02; Palmqvist 2020 rho=0.64 vs 0.15-NS split by amyloid status) WITHOUT gating the spatial PATTERN itself (Vogel 2020: connectome-ESM fits tau topology irrespective of amyloid status) -- an unreconciled hidden-variable tension.

The amyloid-tau spatial correlation strength itself disagrees by cohort scale/composition: weak r=0.18 in Ossenkoppele 2016's small (n=16), phenotype-diverse, amyloid-negative-control-inclusive sample vs strong r=0.65-0.81 in Hu et al 2026's large (n=438), mostly-typical-amnestic-AD sample -- reported as a genuine disclosed tension, not smoothed over.

Tau-PET tracer (AV-1451/flortaucipir) off-target binding to neuromelanin, choroid-plexus calcification, vessels, and substantia nigra is directly documented (Marquie 2015, Lowe 2016) -- a real measurement caveat; attenuation-bias reasoning argues this should WEAKEN not manufacture the tau-beats-amyloid finding, but that reasoning is not itself a new empirical datapoint.

The Part 2 network-diffusion geometric model is an explicitly-disclosed hand-specified TOY graph (10 nodes, 14 literature-informed but not DTI-derived edges) -- its role is mechanism-demonstration (hierarchical topology + correct epicenter is SUFFICIENT to reproduce stereotyped order from first principles), not a claim of connectomic precision; the real external magnitude anchor is Vogel et al 2020 (n=312, 70% variance).

No single cohort in this dossier jointly measures autopsy-Braak-stage AND connectome-ESM-fit AND biochemical-seeding-assay in the SAME subjects -- the 4 spatial-spread legs corroborate across different cohorts, the same disclosed limitation already present in this repo's own prior-session NEU-TAU-PROPAGATION graph-node design.

Brier et al 2016's headline same-cohort quote ('tau... was a better predictor of cognitive performance than Abeta... in any region') is verified verbatim but is qualitative -- the abstract does not print the underlying r/beta statistic, so it is used as a corroborating, not a quantitative, leg.

The adversarial dissent-search (hunting for a same-cohort finding where amyloid beats tau at tracking cognition) was a targeted 3-query search this session, not a systematic review -- absence-of-finding is reported exactly as that, an honest negative search result, not proof no such finding exists in the wider literature.

The UCSF-site convergence count was deliberately DE-INFLATED (3 papers sharing the same Rabinovici/Jagust-affiliated recruitment base counted as ONE site, not three) to avoid a common-mode over-count -- a correction against the claim's apparent strength, disclosed for transparency.
